problems.stem: A rectangle has width b and height h. Its centroidal area moment of inertia is bh³/12. What is its moment of inertia about the base?
options: bh³/3 (centroidal value plus the parallel-axis correction A × d² = bh × (h/2)² = bh³/4).
problems.explanation: Parallel-axis theorem: I_base = I_c + A × d² = bh³/12 + bh × (h/2)² = bh³/12 + bh³/4 = bh³/3.

problems.stem: Among all axes parallel to a given direction, which axis through the body has the minimum moment of inertia?
options: The centroidal axis. The parallel-axis theorem I = I_c + Ad² makes the Ad² term non-negative, so I_c is the minimum.
The axis farthest from the centroid.
All parallel axes give the same I.
problems.explanation: Ad² is non-negative, so any non-centroidal parallel axis adds to I_c. The centroidal axis is uniquely the minimum.

problems.stem: Which units distinguish the area moment of inertia from the mass moment of inertia?
options: Area moment of inertia: m⁴ (geometric, used in statics for bending). Mass moment of inertia: kg·m² (dynamics, used in τ = Iα). Reading the units prevents confusing the two.
problems.explanation: Different physical quantities sharing the symbol I. Units disambiguate them.

problems.stem: A triangular distributed load ramps from 0 at one end to w₀ at the other end of a beam of length L. The equivalent concentrated force is:
options: w₀L/2 (the area under the triangle) acting at 2L/3 from the zero end (the centroid of a triangle with apex at the zero end).
problems.explanation: The equivalent force magnitude equals the area under the load curve; its location is the centroid of that area. For a triangle: F = w₀L/2 at x = 2L/3.
